Two fixed load-sharing -48 VDC supplies, no fans at all, filter slot blanked. The datasheet's ordering section lists the base model and no variants, so there is one row and it carries no part number.","kind":"base","part-numbers":{"AS5915-16X":{}}}},"description":"4x 10G SFP+, 8x 1G SFP and 4x 1G RJ-45 fanless cell site gateway, sold as the CSR180, Broadcom BCM88273 Qumran-UX with an Intel Atom C3308 and a Stratum 3E OCXO. The CSR200's shell with no fans in it: passively cooled behind a honeycombed faceplate, needing at least 1 m/s of external airflow, with no FAN lamp and no BITS port. Ports number from 1; all timing, management and power connections are on the front, and the two DC supplies are fixed.","format":1,"gaps":[{"reason":"sources-disagree","scope":["front"],"wanted":"A figure or drawing of this faceplate that can carry a dimension. THE ONE THAT EXISTS CANNOT, AND THE PROOF IS A STANDARD IT CONTRADICTS. Its SFP cage pitch reads 14.7-14.75 measured two ways - across the four cage bores and across the shell walls between them - against the SFF-8432 figure of 14.25 that the registry carries and that the CSR200's figure reproduces at 14.22. Its RJ-45 cell pitch reads 14.4 against a registry 13.97, the same three percent high. And its DC terminal blocks read about eleven percent SMALL against the sibling's. Nothing reconciles those with one scale. THE OBVIOUS EXPLANATION WAS TESTED AND FAILED. A perspective render would taper: panel height sampled along x is flat on both faces, 425-419 px across the CSR200 and 425-430 across this one, and the CSR180's absolute feature POSITIONS line up with the CSR200's to a millimetre or two over the whole 440. What is wrong is local scale, not geometry - the art is honeycomb dark-on-dark at low contrast and repeated careful reads of one feature wobble by 0.5 to 1 mm where the CSR200's repeat to 0.05. WHAT WAS DONE ABOUT IT: every standard part takes its size from the registry - SFP 14.25, RJ-45 13.97, USB-A, SMB - and the figure supplies POSITIONS and COUNTS only. That is the division docs/modelling-a-device.md already draws for ganged pitch, applied to the whole face. The two non-standard parts, common/dc-terminal-24@1 and edgecore/filter-slot-5915-16x@1, are sized from edge POSITIONS for the same reason, and each says so.","what":"figure-fidelity"},{"reason":"needs-photo","scope":["front"],"wanted":"Which of the four stacked RJ-45 positions is which. The face carries two 1x2 stacks - four jacks - and the datasheet names only THREE non-traffic RJ-45s: the console (callout 4), the ToD/1PPS (callout 10) and the management port (callout 11). There is no BITS port on this model, which is the CSR200's callout 4 and the reason that device has twelve callouts and this one eleven. The silkscreen under the left stack is a single lamp and legend where the CSR200 has two, and it is not legible at 9.63 px/mm. So the fourth position is either blank or something unlisted, and the three that are named are placed here in the CSR200's order - console top right, management bottom right, ToD/1PPS bottom left - which is an INFERENCE FROM THE SIBLING, not a reading.","what":"management-stack-assignment"},{"reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["rear","top","bottom","left","right"],"wanted":"A figure of any face but the front. Neither document draws one. The quick start's step 3 does picture the grounding point - a two-hole lug on the SIDE panel near the rear, with the earth symbol beside it - which is more than the CSR200's quick start gives, but a three-quarter view of a corner fixes no coordinate, so the lug is not placed. The side panels matter more here than on any other device in this family: this box is cooled by air someone else moves across it.","what":"rear-elevation"},{"reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["front"],"wanted":"An LED table. Neither document has one, and unlike the CSR200's quick start this one does not even state that the PSU lamps come up green. Five system lamps are legible - LOC, DIAG, PSU1, PSU2, ALARM - and every lamp here carries `off` and one green `on`, borrowed from edgecore/csr200 where a quick-start sentence supports it. Borrowed, and said to be.","what":"led-vocabularies"},{"reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["front"],"wanted":"Which of each optical port's two bezel lamps is link and which is activity - the same silence as on the CSR200, from the same vendor, about the same bezel.","what":"port-lamp-roles"},{"reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["front"],"wanted":"Whether an air filter is sold for this model at all. SIX ARE THE COAX LEGENDS, as on edgecore/csr200 and for the same reason: each timing pair prints `IN OUT` on one baseline with `1PPS` or `10MHz` under it, and the legend is centred on the PAIR while the rule measures each word against the single jack it names. Moving them onto the jack centres would put the legend across the jacks. TWO ARE `Input-`, 0.7 and 1.0 mm right of their block's centre, and that is where the metal puts them: common/dc-terminal-24@1's three poles sit about 0.9 mm right of the body centre - an asymmetry measured on all four blocks across both devices and recorded on the part - so a label centred on its POLE is necessarily off-centre against the BODY. The rule compares it with the body. TWO ARE RJ-45 NUMERAL GROUPS, centred on their metal cell while the rule compares them with the 8P8C bore, which is not centred in a rj45-ganged cell."}},"manufacturer":"Edgecore","maturity":"modelled","model":"AS5915-16X","name":"csr180","portfolio":{"family":"Cell Site Router","line":"Service Provider","series":"CSR180"},"profile":"networking","provenance":{"chassis":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet - \"Dimensions (WxDxH): 440 x 240 x 44 mm (17.32 x 9.45 x 1.73 in)\" and \"Weight: 3.8 kg (8.38 lb), with two installed PSUs\", both identical to the CSR200's. The quick start does not restate them. 440 is the body width: \"Installations to standard 19\", 21\" and 23\" rack\" makes the brackets an accessory outside it."},"cooling":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"THIS BOX HAS NO FANS AND THAT IS WHY THE FACEPLATE LOOKS LIKE THIS. The datasheet calls the AS5915-16X a fanless, passively cooled platform and asks that it be deployed in external airflow, front-to-back or back-to-front, of at least 1 m/s measured at any point on the product surface. So `airflow: passive` rather than a direction - the datasheet names both directions as acceptable and neither as the product's - and the front plate is honeycombed edge to edge where the CSR200's is solid with perforated columns. It is also why there is no FAN lamp: five system lamps are printed, LOC DIAG PSU1 PSU2 ALARM, with the CSR200's FAN position simply empty."},"figure-choice":{"confidence":"measured","note":"Gate 1. Page 2 rendered at 600 dpi; panel found by row/column darkness at (364,1199)-(4600,1628), 4237 x 430 px, aspect 9.8535 against 10.0 for 440/44 - 1.47 percent out, which is BETTER than the CSR200's 1.86 and is not the point. See the `figure-fidelity` gap: the aspect passes and the art still will not carry a dimension, which is a case docs/modelling-a-device.md's four-percent rule does not cover. Positions it does carry, and positions are what is taken. THE QUICK START HAS NO ELEVATION. Its only hardware drawing is step 3's grounding illustration, a three-quarter view of the rear corner. That is the source for the lug being on the side panel and for nothing else."},"optical-lamps":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"Four lamps per optical column, as on the CSR200: `(down) (up) (down) (up)` in the bezel between the rows, two for the upper port and two for the lower.
